long_biography.plain_text:
Dimitris Procopiou entered commercial shipping with his brother George in 1974, when they co-founded Sea Traders. The brothers expanded from an early bulker into tankers and heavy-lift vessels, and by 1988 controlled 30 debt-free ships. They then divided the fleet equally for family reasons. Dimitris took 15 vessels and later established Centrofin Management, making his shipping fortune self-made rather than inherited.

Centrofin became a private, family-run maritime group operating crude-oil tankers, product carriers and dry-bulk vessels through technical managers Marine Trust and Trust Bulkers. Its official website reports more than 100 vessels operated since 1992 and a current fleet of 44 ships exceeding five million deadweight tonnes. A direct industry interview identifies Procopiou as Centrofin's founder, while recent reporting continues to connect the company with him and with major tanker acquisitions and Kamsarmax newbuildings.
